Some basic math.

Currently of the 32TN of marketable debt roughly 7TN is bills and paying market rates and exposed to higher rates.  Over the next 10 years 17TN of the remaining 25TN refinances at market rates.  Plus we are adding debt and exposed to its rate based on Deficits of roughly 2.2TN over the next 10 years.   The focus on the existing debt refi and its exposure to interest rates seems disproportional to the actual problem of 22TN of new deficits.   20-30% of the "problem" is existing debt costs.

tweets.text:
Imagine Celestial ($MRVL acquisition) was public. 

The valuation would probably be astronomical in US markets (if I had to guess, $6-10B)

Because 2028 revenue projections were $500m (q4 annualized runrate), 2029 revenue projections were $1B.

And because Celestial is a core part of hyperscaler CPO programs. 

Celestial's 2026 Q2 earnings would have been:

- Close to $0 revenue (Marvell said "revenue and earnings since the acquisition were not material")
-  Losing -$12.5M/quarter ($50M/year)

Would people who knew what they were talking about looking at qualification cycle players say...

1. based on Celestial's Q2 P/S numbers and because it was losing -$12.5M a quarter... That it's a worthless meme stock? 

Or 

2. with CPO hyperscaler opportunities for 2028, it should be valued at $6-10B? 

And I think that's a core cultural disagreement between US / EU cultures + markets. 

If you knew how to evaluate qualification cycle players, which number actually matters? I'd argue overwhelmingly the latter.

tweets.text:
Lots of bear posts on the timeline, which is to be expected as there is still an ongoing battle between those who believe we’ve had a trend shift and those who believe we still have our low to come. 

From a technical point of view we don’t have strict confirmation. 

But, I am still in the bulls camp.

A lot of those in the bear camp point to the 4 year cycle, without understanding cycle theory. 

There is room either side of the 4 year mark for a cycle bottom. This is perfectly fine, so isn’t a reason to remain a bear and on the sidelines by itself, which is where I think there is confusion. 

Perfectly trusting exact historical patterns (exact bottom of 12 months of bear) doesn’t overwhelm market context for me. I would even call Bessent’s intervention a kind of white swan, which forced an impulse to set up a slightly earlier 4 year cycle low. 

For me as a bull, invalidation and new macro low would be caused by some sort of cataclysmic drop in the stock market, some macro crisis, or some horrible new event unique to Bitcoin which is unforeseeable. 

82k is the final level which bears have to hold onto, or they are extinct for another cycle.

I think we will still have to endure another drop where everyone questions everything. 200D MA will likely get tested, and everyone that said they wanted to buy the dip won’t actually buy because they will believe in lower prices once we are down there.

Allocating before you have confirmation of a trend shift has always paid very well historically, because you are taking on the risk of being underwater/wrong, and when we finally turn you are set up strongly. 

Obviously doing this too early is a bad idea, but we were in the timing band for a low, so R/R was very much in the favour of long term buyers. 

If you don’t have conviction in this asset class, or the specific high quality assets we have in crypto (not many) then I understand why you don’t want to buy/hold without confirmation.

One thing has always remained true across all cycles is holders of the best assets in crypto who ride the volatility from despair/denial to euphoria make incredible returns. 

It takes actual conviction to do this.

This time won’t be different. 

We have a long way to go.

$TSM Vice President of Advanced Packaging:

"Foundries can scale up the optical engine, but the real bottlenecks to large scale deployment lie elsewhere...

Including lasers, optical fiber, fiber-optic connectors, and test" (UDN)

Lasers: $LITE, $SIVE, $COHR, LandMark (3081), LuxNet, Sumitomo, Furukawa
Optical fiber / FAU: Foci, Browave, $GLW, Sumitomo
Fiber Optic / CPO Connectors: BizLink, $GLW , Fujikura, Nextronics, COXOC

eg. "Foxconn unit ShunSin confirms TSMC COUPE partnership"

I don't think there's anything too new vs. H1, aside from ongoing news (eg. FAU looks like there will have a demand imbalance in 2027, from a report last week). 

But it's helpful to reiterate overall beneficiaries from time to time...

ESMT (3006) is 1.9x P/E ratio off July's earnings annualized. 

Latest net income was: $109M net income/July, which is ~$1.3B annualized. With ~$395.9M net cash and with $249.6M in inventory.

The market cap less net cash and inventory is equivalent to: 

~17 months of July earnings.

Where monetizing that inventory benefits from rising memory prices. 

Their ASP hike expectations were +105–113% Q/Q last quarter from other analyst notes. 

DDR2/DDR3, NOR Flash, SLC NAND, prices are expected to keep rising H2. 

The main question is duration, but I personally think legacy DRAM/NAND shortages tightens throughout 2027. Others might disagree. 

Other analysts like Huanan argue that PSMC wafer hikes are largely pass through (we'll find out H2). 

Most people are finding companies with ~20 forward P/E ending 2028 to be attractive...

But 1.9x current runrate P/E seems like an anomaly to me personally. 

That's my take on the company/legacy memory theme, I'll let others/markets decide if that's undervalued.

there is no good reason to build your modular chain anywhere else and there are, instead, many reasons not to

the current, absurdly low fees to do this (without having to pay to run your own consensus) are a feature, not a bug

expect many, many more L2s to come in the next few years
